content: Resetting priorities for Day 3 of the life of BonBon. I have gotten messages from friends who are thinking about how to create a Markdown web site of their own. I want to share interesting examples showing how people have done it. So here's the first one. We spent a fair amount of time getting Scripting News to be part of this experiment. We wrote a server app that watches what's going on, via the RSS 2.0 feed. When it sees a new or updated post, it generates a Markdown file and updates the toc.opml file to link it into the chronology of the blog. It also recognizes some custom front matter values, and handles special cases for Markdown itself. For example, an image that appears at the beginning of a paragraph, before anything else, is shown in the right margin, like the beautiful Lab in the right margin. It also has a special syntax for inline images, like the one in this post. There's a general config file alongside toc.opml in the .well-known folder at the top level. Also they can be nested, so you could have a .well-known folder at any level. Anyway all this is to say that we've shared a snapshot of the scripting website in markdown in the BonBon repo. More of these to come, and we want to see new examples from people working on this stuff so we can share them with the community. This like coming up with a platform and sharing developer stories.
